title: <KeepAlive>: Component Instance Caching, LRU Eviction, and onActivated Hooks

progressiveExplaining.eli5: When you switch tabs in a web app, the old tab usually gets destroyed and throws away all your typed text. `<KeepAlive>` is like putting the old tab in a suspended hibernation pod: it freezes its memory, DOM, and scroll position. When you click back to that tab, it wakes up instantly in 0ms without re-fetching or resetting your forms.
progressiveExplaining.junior: `<KeepAlive>` is a built-in component that caches inactive component instances instead of destroying them. When switching dynamic components (`<component :is="view">`), wrapped components stay in memory. Instead of `onMounted`/`onUnmounted`, cached components trigger `onActivated()` when shown and `onDeactivated()` when hidden. Use `include`, `exclude`, and `:max="10"` to control caching limits.
progressiveExplaining.senior: Architecturally, `<KeepAlive>` is an internal abstract component that bypasses standard VNode unmounting. When a component wrapped in `<KeepAlive>` is replaced, its DOM sub-tree is detached from the document and retained in an in-memory VNode cache map. When re-activated, the cached VNode instance is re-inserted into the DOM directly. The `:max` prop implements a **Least Recently Used (LRU)** eviction strategy: when cache capacity is exceeded, the oldest inactive instance is permanently unmounted.
progressiveExplaining.underTheHood: In the renderer, `<KeepAlive>` maintains `cache = new Map<CacheKey, VNode>()` and `keys = new Set<CacheKey>()`. On mount, it intercepts `unmount()` by invoking `deactivate(instance, vnode)`. It sets `shapeFlag |= ShapeFlags.COMPONENT_KEPT_ALIVE`. On re-render with a cache hit, `activate()` re-appends `instance.subTree.el` to the parent container and flushes `onActivated` lifecycle hooks through the scheduler post-flush queue.

codeComparison.title: Destroyed Component State vs Cached KeepAlive Instance
codeComparison.summary: Switching tabs without `<KeepAlive>` resets state and re-fetches; `<KeepAlive>` preserves form input and component state.

legacyOrBad.label: Uncached Dynamic Component
legacyOrBad.snippet: <component :is="currentTab" /> // ❌ Destroys state and DOM on every tab switch

fullFile.code:
<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue';
import TabA from './TabA.vue';
import TabB from './TabB.vue';

const currentTab = ref(TabA);
</script>

<template>
  <button @click="currentTab = TabA">Tab A</button>
  <button @click="currentTab = TabB">Tab B</button>
  
  <!-- ❌ TabA is completely destroyed when switching to TabB;
       all form inputs and scroll position in TabA are lost! -->
  <component :is="currentTab" />
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue';
import TabA from './TabA.vue';
import TabB from './TabB.vue';

const currentTab = ref(TabA);
</script>

<template>
  <button @click="currentTab = TabA">Tab A</button>
  <button @click="currentTab = TabB">Tab B</button>
  
  <!-- ✅ NEW: Keeps up to 5 tab instances cached in memory using LRU eviction.
       Form inputs, state, and scroll position remain 100% intact. -->
  <KeepAlive :max="5">
    <component :is="currentTab" />
  </KeepAlive>
</template>

interviewGotchas.question: Do `onMounted` and `onUnmounted` run when a cached `<KeepAlive>` component is toggled back and forth?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Interviewers test your knowledge of KeepAlive-specific lifecycle hooks.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: No. `onMounted` only runs *once* when the component is initially created. When switching away, `onUnmounted` is bypassed and **`onDeactivated`** runs. When returning to the cached component, `onMounted` does *not* run again; instead, **`onActivated`** executes.
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: If you fetch fresh data inside `onMounted()`, a cached KeepAlive component will never re-fetch data on revisit. Move re-validation logic to `onActivated()`.

interviewGotchas.question: What happens when the number of cached components exceeds the `:max` prop?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Checks understanding of the internal cache eviction algorithm.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: `<KeepAlive>` implements a **Least Recently Used (LRU)** eviction policy. When the cache size exceeds `:max`, the component instance that has been inactive for the longest time is evicted from the cache map and permanently unmounted (running its `onUnmounted` hook).
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: Setting `:max` too high can cause excessive memory consumption on mobile devices as dozens of full DOM subtrees remain pinned in RAM.
